column3: Near-exact parallel: believers remember divine favor when hostile hands are restrained.

God's sight of workmanship supplies a general parallel to the focus's closing divine observation.
The ordeal of believers culminates in the assurance that God's help is near.
A small faithful force faces a larger army while trusting victory by God's permission.
Believers under military pressure ask for steadfastness, firm footing, and help against the disbelievers.
Victory over a stronger force comes by God's permission, who repels harm through people.
God explicitly recalls helping the believers at Badr when they were weak.
The believers are promised reinforcement by thousands of angels in battle.
Angelic reinforcement is tied to patience, reverence, and the enemy's advance.
The angelic aid is reassurance; decisive help belongs only to God.
God casts terror into the disbelievers' hearts, showing an unseen reversal of battlefield power.
After anguish, God sends security upon the believers while another group misreads Him under pressure.
God's help makes defeat impossible, while the withdrawal of that help leaves no protector.
The threat of a gathered enemy leads believers to trust God's sufficiency rather than visible numbers.
Direct parallel: God answers believers' plea by reinforcing them with a thousand angels.
Angelic aid brings reassurance and tranquillity while victory remains solely from God.
God announces unseen support to angels and the casting of terror into the enemy.
The verse corrects visible agency in battle: the believers acted, yet God brought the decisive effect.
It identifies divine victory as the answer to the opposing side's demand for judgment.
Believers are told to remember when they were few and afraid, then sheltered and strengthened by God.
God alters each side's visible estimate of the other so that His decreed matter is completed.
In direct battle instruction, steadfastness is joined to abundant remembrance of God.
Obedience, unity, patience, and resistance to failure specify the faithful response under conflict.
God's support is explicitly given through both His victory and the believers.
At Hunayn, numerical strength first deceives believers before the battlefield closes in on them.
Believers answer danger by locating every outcome within God's decree and protection.
The adversary can await only one of two good outcomes for believers, including victory or martyrdom.
God defends the believers, establishing divine protection against hostile betrayal and ingratitude.
Permission to fight the wronged is grounded in God's power to grant them victory.
God promises to support those who support His cause after unjust expulsion.
The promise of security after fear gives a broader fulfillment pattern for divinely protected believers.
The verse states that helping the believers is an obligation God has taken upon Himself.
Immediate continuation denies that flight can rescue the besieged from death or killing.
It denies that anyone can shield people from God's intended harm or mercy.
It exposes those who hinder defense and call others away from the dangerous confrontation.
It portrays the confederates as a continuing visible threat and exposes fearful calculation about them.
Believers see the confederates yet interpret the sight as the fulfilled promise of God and His Messenger.
It identifies believers who remained true to their covenant amid the trial.
Direct resolution: God turns back the confederates without gain and spares believers the fighting.
God explicitly promises support to His messengers and believers in worldly life and at the testimony.
Helping God's cause is answered with God's help and the strengthening of believers' feet.
Believers are told not to weaken or seek compromise while God is with them.
God's knowledge of what was in believers' hearts brings tranquillity and a near victory.
Promised gains and the restraint of hostile hands show divine control over an apparent victory.
God encompasses another victory not yet within the believers' power or sight.
If the disbelievers fought, they would turn away and find neither protector nor helper.
God restrains hands in Mecca because unseen believers could otherwise be harmed.
God sends tranquillity upon the Messenger and believers while the disbelievers remain in partisan rage.
The hostile force is foretold to be defeated and turn its backs.
God decrees that He and His messengers will prevail, grounding victory in divine power.
God overturns reliance on visible fortifications by coming from where the defenders did not expect and casting terror.
Believers are promised help from God and a near victory as glad news.
God, Gabriel, righteous believers, and angels are named as support for the Messenger.
The arrival of God's help and victory provides the broad fulfillment counterpart to threatened believers' deliverance.
